subject: CAIQ scope partition & proof staging plan
messages:
From: Claire Barnes <claire@aurorahealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: security@aurorahealth.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ: partial scope (inference runtime + telemetry) - initial ask

Hi Tessa / Jonas,

Thanks again for taking this on. For the upcoming CSA evaluation we need a CAIQ crosswalk limited to two domains: inference runtime (model serving, KV cache, quantization controls) and telemetry/observability (ingest, retention, access controls). Our assessor asked for: 1) a concise mapping from CAIQ questions to Redwood controls, and 2) three representative artifacts per control (logs, config snapshots, runbooks).

I attached a short questions doc with a couple of clarifications about scope (initial_questions.pdf). Can you confirm whether you can:
- provide an annotated CAIQ spreadsheet mapping (question -> Redwood control + owner)
- stage artifacts in a short-lived bucket or shared Drive link for our reviewers
- suggest a minimal sample set (we're fine with sampling rather than exhaustive exports)

We're working to lock the audit window the week of Dec 6 — would a delivery by Nov 24 work for a first pass? If not, propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Claire Barnes
Security Lead, Aurora Health

---
Attachment: initial_questions.pdf (3 pages, scope clarifications)
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Claire Barnes <claire@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ: partial scope (inference runtime + telemetry) - initial ask

Claire — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. We can support this scope with a focused plan. Proposed approach:

1) Scope partition & owner assignment (by EOD Monday, Nov 15)
   - Inference runtime: Jonas Weber (runtime controls, KV/cache, quantization)
   - Telemetry & retention: Marissa Cole (logs, traces, retention/service accounts)

2) Deliverables (first pass by Nov 22):
   - Annotated CAIQ spreadsheet mapping question -> Redwood control -> owner -> short narrative (1–2 lines)
   - Proof index: a single xlsx that lists artifact filenames, short description, control id, and URL/Drive path (rwd-proof-index-template.xlsx)
   - Telemetry sample list: CSV with three representative log exports and redaction notes (telemetry-sample-list.csv)

3) Artifact staging & access
   - We'll stage artifacts in a time-limited Drive folder and provide signed download links. If the assessor prefers a storage bucket, we can do presigned URLs.

4) Sampling strategy & privacy
   - We will include redacted logs where necessary and a redaction statement in the proof index. Any PII found will be removed; we will note redaction methods.

5) Timeline & checkpoints
   - Nov 15: internal owner confirmation + control split (deliverable: owner roster)
   - Nov 22: first pass annotated CAIQ + proof index + two sample artifacts per priority control
   - Nov 29: final artifacts and any follow-ups to support the audit window starting Dec 6

Questions for you:
- Is there any specific residency or data residency requirement for the artifacts aside from standard Aurora controls?
- Do you want us to include runtime metrics (latency/cold-start traces) as artifacts, or keep artifacts strictly config/logs?

I'll attach the proof-index template and a calendar invite that proposes brief internal syncs. Jon and Marissa — can you confirm ownership and the Nov 22 first-pass commitment?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: rwd-proof-index-template.xlsx, sample-rotation-calendar.ics
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ: partial scope (inference runtime + telemetry) - initial ask

Acked — I'll take telemetry ownership. Quick clarifications:

1) Retention period to surface: do we show the standard 90-day retention for debug logs or the longer 13-month retention used for billing traces? For the assessor I suggest 90-day debug + example of 13-month billing trace with a redaction note.

2) For artifacts I plan to include:
   - service-logs-2026-10-01-to-2026-10-07.log (redacted) — example of ingestion + retention
   - telemetry-config-20261101.json — exporter config + retention policy
   - observability-runbook-runtime.pdf — runbook snippet referencing access controls and escalation

I'll prepare the telemetry-sample-list.csv and drop the staged links in the proof index. Nov 22 first pass is feasible, but I'll need the drive permissions by Nov 15 (Tessa — please share the folder ACL once created).

Marissa Cole
Principal Observability Engineer — Redwood Inference

---
Attachment references: service-logs-2026-10-01-to-2026-10-07.log (redacted), telemetry-config-20261101.json, observability-runbook-runtime.pdf
From: Claire Barnes <claire@aurorahealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: security@aurorahealth.com, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ: partial scope (inference runtime + telemetry) - initial ask

Thanks — this plan looks good and the timeline aligns with our audit window. A couple quick notes:
- Residency: artifacts can be in your Drive (no additional residency constraints).
- Runtime metrics: yes, please include a short sample (latency histogram or cold-start trace) as an optional artifact — that helps our performance-related controls.

I'll accept the calendar invite and book a 30-minute review with the assessor for Nov 24 if possible. Looking forward to the first pass on Nov 22.

Claire Barnes
Security Lead, Aurora Health

---
Requested next actions: Tessa to create Drive folder + share ACL (by Nov 15); Jon to prepare runtime control notes; Marissa to stage telemetry samples and upload proof index row entries.
